title: The Senate Debates Caesar
setting: The Senate house in Rome. Caesar's letter has been read: he will lay down his command if Pompey lays down his. The tribunes Antony and Cassius have vetoed every motion against him. Outside the walls, Pompey has legions and Caesar is at Ravenna with one.
stakes: Whether the Senate votes the final decree and makes civil war certain, or finds a formula that lets both men climb down.

roles_in_scene.cicero: Newly returned from Cilicia, desperate for a compromise, and trusted by nobody on either side
roles_in_scene.cato-the-younger: Refusing every accommodation, as he has for ten years, and about to be proved right in the worst way
roles_in_scene.pompey: Insisting he wants no war while declining to disarm first
roles_in_scene.mark-antony: Tribune of the plebs, vetoing on Caesar's behalf, and days from fleeing the city

ground_truth: Caesar's offer of mutual disarmament is put to the house and treated as a manoeuvre rather than an offer
Cato refuses any settlement that leaves Caesar a command or a consulship in absentia
Cicero proposes compromise formulas and finds no support from either side
Pompey lets it be known he will not disarm first, while denying he wants war
The senatus consultum ultimum is passed and the tribunes' veto is overridden
Antony and Cassius flee Rome for Caesar's camp
opening_line: A letter has been read aloud. Every man in the chamber understands that the next few hours decide whether there is a war.
sources: Plutarch, Lives of Caesar, Pompey, Cato the Younger
